title: Line spectra, the Bohr model, and matter waves
objective: Use signed energy changes for hydrogen transitions and explain the roles of matter waves and uncertainty.

blocks.alt: Schematic parallels show hydrogen energy levels from n equals 1 to 5 and the zero-energy ionization limit. A downward arrow runs from n equals 4 to 2.
blocks.caption: Schematic energy ladder. Spacing decreases as $n$ rises. The downward $4\to2$ transition emits a Balmer photon.

blocks.title: Common errors
blocks.md: Use final minus initial for the atom. Use positive photon energy. Orbital drawings describe probability; a classical trajectory cannot be read from them.

blocks.title: Exam practice
blocks.md: When comparing transitions, compare differences of inverse squares. Remember that a larger energy gap means a shorter wavelength.

blocks.title: Hydrogen energy levels and spectra
blocks.focus: Name the initial and final levels and assign absorption or emission before calculating.

blocks.title: Hydrogen emission from 4 to 2
blocks.problem: Compute the atom’s energy change and emitted wavelength for $n=4\to2$.

steps.title: Subtract
steps.why: Ending at a lower level gives a negative atomic change.

steps.title: Convert
steps.md: Multiply the meter result by $10^9$ nm/m.
steps.why: The answer is in the visible Balmer series.
